Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:1.hebrew: מאי שנא - עדות מעריות, דאמר לקמן בפרק נושאין (יבמות דף צח.), גר שהיה נשוי אחותו מן האם, יוציא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:1.english: What is the difference - [between] testimony and forbidden relations, as it states later in the chapter [entitled] Nos'in (Yevamot 98a): "A convert who was married to his maternal sister must divorce [her]."

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:2.hebrew: לכל מסורה - הכל נושאין נשים. הלכך, אי שרית לקיומה, אתי נמי למישרי ערוה בישראל, דכולי עלמא לא ידעי דטעמא דגר משום דכקטן שנולד דמי:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:2.english: Handed over to all - Everyone marries wives. Therefore, if you permit [him] to keep her, [people] will also come to permit a forbidden relation among [born] Jews, for not everyone knows that the reason [in the case] of a convert is because he is like a newborn child.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:3.hebrew: לבית דין מסורה - ואי נמי מכשרת עדות אחים גרים, לא אתיא לאכשורי אחין ישראל, דבית דין ידעי דגר שנתגייר כקטן שנולד דמי:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:10:3.english: Is handed over to the court - Even if you validate the testimony of convert brothers, it will not come to validate [born] Jewish brothers, for the court knows that a convert who converted is like a newborn child.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:1.english: A brother of any kind - [It] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:2.english: And [he is] his brother in all respects - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:3.hebrew: שפחה ועובדת כוכבים - ולדה כמוה ובתרה אזיל, כדיליף בגמ':
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:3.english: A maidservant and an idolatress - Her child is like her and follows after her [status], as [it] derives in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:4.hebrew: על מכתו ועל קללתו - אם הכה או קלל את אביו, חייב מיתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:11:4.english: For striking him and for cursing him - If he struck or cursed his father, he is liable to death.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:13:1.hebrew: מדלענין יבום מיפטר - את אשת אביו מיבום פוטר, כגון אם היה לו בן ממזר ונשא אשה ומת ולא ילדה לו, פטורה מן היבום בשביל הממזר בן בעלה, כדיליף לקמן: "בן אין לו" — עיין עליו:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:13:1.english: Since with regard to levirate marriage, [he] exempts - He exempts his father's wife from levirate marriage; for example, if [a man] had a son who was a mamzer, and he married a woman and died, and she had not borne [children] to him, she is exempt from levirate marriage on account of the mamzer, her husband's son, as [the Gemara] derives later: "He has no child" — investigate [concerning] him.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:1:1.hebrew: הנך תרתי דדמיין להדדי - אשת אחי אבי האב ואחות אבי האב, שהן צד אחוה דאב, ולמטה דידהו ערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:1:1.english: Those two that are similar to each other - The wife of the father's father's brother and the sister of the father's father, which are [on] the sibling side of the father, and below them is a forbidden relationship.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:1.hebrew: שלישי שבבנו - בת בן בנו, דהא בת בנו ערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:1.english: The third [generation] from his son - [That is,] the daughter of his son's son, for his son's daughter is a forbidden relationship [by Torah law].

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:2.hebrew: ושבבתו - בת בן בתו, שהרי בת בתו ערוה; הלכך, בת בן בתו שניה. וכן בת בן בנה של אשתו או בת בן בתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:2.english: And from his daughter - [This refers to] the daughter of his daughter's son, for his daughter's daughter is an ervah [a biblically forbidden relationship]; therefore, the daughter of his daughter's son is a sheniyah [a secondary forbidden relationship]. And similarly, the daughter of his wife's son's son, or the daughter of her daughter's son.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:3.hebrew: רביעי שבחמיו - דור רביעי שבחמיו, היינו אם אם חמיו, והוא דור רביעי לאשתו, ואשתו בכלל:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:3.english: The fourth [generation] from his father-in-law - The fourth generation from his father-in-law, that is, the mother of his father-in-law's mother; and it is the fourth generation from his wife, with his wife included [in the count].

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:4.english: And from his mother-in-law - [This refers to] the mother of his mother-in-law's mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:5.hebrew: שניה - דאם חמיו ואם חמותו ערוה, שהן בכלל אשה ובת בנה, אשה ובת בתה; הלכך אמו שניה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:2:5.english: A secondary [forbidden relationship] - For the mother of his father-in-law and the mother of his mother-in-law are ervah [biblically forbidden], as they are included in "a woman and her son's daughter" [or] "a woman and her daughter's daughter"; therefore, his mother is a secondary [forbidden relationship].

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:3:1.hebrew: מאי שנא למעלה - דקרי לאם אם חמיו ואם אם חמותו רביעי, וקא חשיב לאשתו בחושבנא דדרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:3:1.english: What is different above - Where he calls the mother of the mother of his father-in-law and the mother of the mother of his mother-in-law "fourth [generation]," and he counts his wife in the reckoning of the generations.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:3:2.english: And what is different below - That he calls the daughter of his son's son [the] third generation, and does not count his wife so that she would be [the] fourth.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:3:3.hebrew: לאו מכח אשתו קאתי - אלא מכח דידיה, דבבנו מאנוסה עסקינן:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:3:3.english: [The prohibition] does not stem from his wife - Rather, [it stems] from himself, for we are dealing with his son from a woman he raped.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:6:1.hebrew: לההיא מתניתא - הא דקתני לעיל "מה הן שניות", בההיא איירי רב, ואמר: ארבע יש להן הפסק ותו לא, אבל בהנך דר' חייא איכא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:6:1.english: To that baraita - The one that teaches above, "What are the secondary [forbidden relatives]?" Rav was speaking regarding that [baraita], and he said [that] four have a conclusion and no more, but regarding those of Rabbi Chiyya, there are [more].

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:6:2.hebrew: ת"ש - דתני בשניות דר' חייא: שלישי שבבנו ורביעי שבחמיו, ותו לא. אלמא יש להם הפסק:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:6:2.english: Come and hear - For it was taught in [the baraita of] secondary forbidden relationships of Rabbi Chiya: "the third [generation] of his son and the fourth [generation] of his father-in-law" — and no more. Thus, they have a limit.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:7:1.hebrew: בגרים - גזרו שניות, שאם היה גר נשוי אם אמו, יוציא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:7:1.english: For converts - [Did] they issue a decree [regarding] secondary [forbidden relationships], [meaning] that if a convert was married to his mother's mother, he must divorce [her]?

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:8:1.english: From a more stringent sanctity - For idolaters are warned against forbidden relationships.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:8:2.english: The Sages would not have decreed regarding them - For [a convert] is like a newborn child and has no kinship.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:9:1.hebrew: לא יעידו - לכתחלה, דקורבת אם בגרים קורבה היא, דהא ודאי אמו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:9:1.english: They may not testify - [That is,] ab initio, because maternal kinship among converts is [considered] kinship, since she is certainly his mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:9:2.english: And if they testified, their testimony is valid - Because [a convert] is like a newborn child.

Rashi on Yevamot 22a:9:3.hebrew: מעידין לכתחלה - דרחמנא אפקריה לזרע מצרי, דכתיב: "זרמת סוסים זרמתם" (יחזקאל כ״ג:כ׳), הלכך קורבת אב אינה קורבה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22a:9:3.english: They may testify ab initio - For the Merciful One declared the seed of an Egyptian [i.e., a gentile] ownerless, as it is written: "the issue of horses is their issue" (Ezekiel 23:20); therefore, paternal kinship is not [considered] kinship.

Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:10:1.hebrew: ערוה לכל מסורה - תימה, דלעיל קאמר דטעמא דגרים שלא יאמרו: "באנו מקדושה" כו', והכא משמע טעמא משום דאתיא לאיחלופי בישראל, כדפי' בקונטרס. וכן בפ' נושאין (לקמן יבמות דף צז: ושם) משמע דטעמא משום איחלופי, גבי בני יודן אמתא אישתחרור, שרא להו רב אחא בר יעקב למינסב נשי דהדדי, וקאמר: מן האם ולא מן האב — כולי עלמא לא פליגי דאסור; מן האב ולא מן האם — כולי עלמא לא פליגי דמותר; כי פליגי — מן האב ומן האם. ואי משום "שמא יאמרו", אמאי שרי התם מן האב ומן האם? אבל אי משום איחלופי — ניחא, דכיון דאיכא נמי צד אב, לא אתי לאיחלופי, דבתר אב שדי להו; ומצרים אין להם קורבת אב, דכתיב: "וזרמת סוסים זרמתם", ולא שייך למיגזר אטו ישראל. ויש לומר דהני תרי טעמי צריכין: דבקורבת אב שהיו אסורין קודם — לא שייך טעמא לאיחלופי, שהכל יודעים דרחמנא אפקריה לזרעיה, כגון אשת אביו לרבי עקיבא ואחות אביו לרבי אליעזר, דאמר בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נח.): "על כן יעזב איש את אביו ואת אמו" — ר' אליעזר אומר: אחות אביו, ור"ע אומר: אשת אביו — הוי טעמא שלא יאמרו כו'. אבל אשת אביו לרבי אליעזר ואחות אביו לרבי עקיבא — שרי, דלא משום "שמא יאמרו" איכא ולא משום איחלופי איכא. אבל עריות שמצד אם, שלא היו אסורות קודם — יש לאסור משום איחלופי, דמשום "שמא יאמרו" ליכא. והא דאמר בפרק ד' מיתות (ג"ז שם): "נשא אחותו מן האם — יוציא", היינו משום איחלופי, ד"שמא יאמרו" ליכא, שלא היו נאסרות בגיותם; ומן האב — יקיים, דמשום איחלופי ליכא בצד אב, כדפרישית. והיינו טעמא נמי דאמר: אחין מן האם לא יעידו לכתחלה, דלמא אתי לאיחלופי, אבל מן האב — יעידו לכתחלה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:10:1.english: Forbidden relations are handed over to all - This is puzzling, for earlier [the Gemara] stated that the reason [for prohibiting certain relatives] of converts is so that they will not say, "We have come from [a higher] sanctity [to a lower sanctity]," etc., whereas here it implies that the reason is because it might come to be confused with a [born] Jew, as Rashi explained. And similarly, in the chapter [entitled] Nose'in (below, Yevamot 97b and there [on 98a]), it implies that the reason is because of confusion [with born Jews], regarding [the case where] the sons of Yudan the maidservant were emancipated, [and] Rav Acha bar Yaakov permitted them to marry each other's [former] wives, and [the Gemara] states: [Where they are brothers] from the mother and not from the father — everyone agrees that it is forbidden; from the father and not from the mother — everyone agrees that it is permitted; where they disagree [is when they are brothers both] from the father and from the mother. Now if [the reason were] because of "lest they say [we came from a higher sanctity to a lower sanctity]," why is it permitted there [when they are brothers] from the father and from the mother? However, if [it is] because of confusion [with born Jews], it is understandable: since there is also a paternal side, it will not come to be confused [with a born Jew], because [people] attribute them to the father — and Egyptians have no paternal kinship, as it is written: "and whose issue is like the issue of horses" (Ezekiel 23:20) — so it is not applicable to decree [a prohibition] on account of [born] Jews. And one can answer that both of these reasons are necessary: for regarding paternal kinship where they were [already] forbidden beforehand [as non-Jews], the reason of confusion does not apply, since everyone knows that the Merciful One has declared his seed ownerless; for example, his father's wife according to Rabbi Akiva and his father's sister according to Rabbi Eliezer — as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 58a): "'Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother' (Genesis 2:24) — Rabbi Eliezer says: [this refers to] his father's sister, and Rabbi Akiva says: [this refers to] his father's wife" — [there] the reason is "so that they will not say," etc. However, his father's wife according to Rabbi Eliezer and his father's sister according to Rabbi Akiva are permitted, since neither the reason of "lest they say" applies nor [the reason of] confusion applies. By contrast, forbidden relations on the mother's side, which were not forbidden beforehand [as non-Jews], must be forbidden because of confusion, since [the reason of] "lest they say" does not apply. And that which [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (there as well [Sanhedrin 58a]): "[If a convert] married his sister from his mother, he must divorce [her]," that is because of confusion, since [the reason of] "lest they say" does not apply, as they were not forbidden during their gentileness; whereas [if she is his sister] from his father, he may keep [her as his wife], since there is no [concern of] confusion on the father's side, as I explained. And this is also the reason that [the Gemara] states: Brothers from the mother should not testify [together] initially, lest it come to be confused [with born Jews], whereas [brothers] from the father may testify [together] initially.

Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:11:1.hebrew: מי שיש לו אח מ"מ זוקק אשת אחיו - בגמרא מפרש: לאתויי ממזר. וא"ת, מרישא שמעינן לה: "בת ישראל לנתין וממזר", דחולצת ולא מתייבמת? ויש לומר דאי מהתם הוי אמינא כששניהם ממזרים, אבל כשאחיו המת כשר, אין אחיו ממזר זוקק אשתו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:11:1.english: "Anyone who has a brother of any kind creates a levirate bond [with] his brother's wife" - In the Gemara it explains [that "of any kind" comes] to include a mamzer. And if you will say: we already learn it from the earlier Mishnah [which states]: "An Israelite woman [married] to a natin or a mamzer" — that she performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage [which already shows that a mamzer creates a levirate bond]? One can answer that if [we derived it only] from there, I would have said [that this applies only] when both of them are mamzerim, but when his deceased brother is of valid lineage, his mamzer brother does not bind his wife [in a levirate bond].

Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:12:1.hebrew: פשיטא אחיו הוא - תימה: אמאי פשיטא ליה? הא איצטריך שפיר לאשמועינן דמחייבי כריתות הוי אחיו, ולא ממעטינן ליה למי שיש אישות לאביך בה, כדפריך לקמן (יבמות דף כג.) לרבי יוסי בר יהודה: "ואימא למי שיש אישות לאביך בה למעוטי חייבי כריתות"? וי"ל דה"מ לשנויי הכי, אלא דניחא ליה לשנויי דאיצטריך משום דהוה ילפינן "אחוה" "אחוה" מבני יעקב — דמשום האי טעמא איצטריך "בן אין לו עיין עליו" דממזר פוטר מן היבום, דלא נימא דנילף "אחוה" "אחוה" מבני יעקב דלא זקיק, ומדלא זקיק — מיפטר נמי לא פטר. ועוד אור"י דהכי פריך: "פשיטא", כיון דתני "אחיו הוא לכל דבר", פשיטא דזוקק נמי ליבום! ומשני דס"ד אע"ג ד"אחיו הוא לכל דבר", ה"א ליבום לא זוקק, משום דילפינן "אחוה" "אחוה" מבני יעקב. ובתר הכי פריך: "ואחיו הוא לכל דבר" — דהיינו ליורשו וליטמא לו — פשיטא! כיון דזוקק ליבום אף על גב דהוה ס"ד למילף מבני יעקב, כ"ש לשאר דברים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:12:1.english: Isn't it obvious? He is his brother - [This is] astonishing: why is it obvious to [the Gemara]? Surely [this teaching] is very much needed to inform us that [a child born] from [unions] liable to karet [excision] is considered his brother, and we do not exclude him [based on the principle of] "to one in whom your father has [a potential for] marriage," just as [the Gemara] asks later (Yevamot 23a) according to Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda: "And say [that the verse] 'to one in whom your father has [a potential for] marriage' comes to exclude [those liable to] karet"? And one can answer that [the Gemara] could have answered thus, except that it preferred to answer that it is needed because we would have derived "brotherhood" [and] "brotherhood" from the sons of Jacob — for because of this reason, [the exposition of] "and he has no child — examine [the matter] regarding him" was needed [to teach] that a mamzer exempts from levirate marriage, so that we would not say that we derive "brotherhood" [and] "brotherhood" from the sons of Jacob that he does not create a levirate bond, and since he does not create a levirate bond, [a mamzer child] does not exempt either. Furthermore, Ri says that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: "Isn't it obvious?" — since [the Mishnah] taught "he is his brother in all respects," it is obvious that he also creates a levirate bond for levirate marriage! And [the Gemara] answers that you might have thought that even though "he is his brother in all respects," I would have said that for levirate marriage he does not create a levirate bond, because we derive "brotherhood" [and] "brotherhood" from the sons of Jacob. And after that, [the Gemara] asks: "And he is his brother in all respects" — which refers to inheriting him and becoming ritually impure for him — isn't that obvious? Since he creates a levirate bond for levirate marriage even though we would have thought to derive from the sons of Jacob [that he does not], all the more so [is he his brother] for other matters.

Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:5:1.hebrew: שניות דרבי חייא יש להן הפסק או לא - תימה, דלעיל תנא דכלת בן בנו אסורה עד סוף כל הדורות, ודומה דכ"ש בת בן בנו עד סוף כל הדורות, שהן קורבי עצמו ולא מחמת קדושין. וי"ל, דכלת בן בנו יש לאוסרו, שהן בני ירושה ושכיחא גביה; אבל בת בני בנים לאו בת ירושה היא, ולא שכיחא גביה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22a:5:1.english: "Do the secondary [relationships] of Rabbi Ḥiyya have a conclusion or not?" - It is puzzling, for earlier it taught that the daughter-in-law of one's son's son is forbidden until the end of all generations, and it would seem that all the more so the daughter of one's son's son [is forbidden] until the end of all generations, since they are one's own relatives and not [related] through betrothal. And one can answer that [in the case of] the daughter-in-law of one's son's son, there is reason to forbid her, since they [the sons' sons] are heirs and she is frequently around him; however, the daughter of one's sons' sons is not an heiress and is not frequently around him.
